title: Cro Sea Villas
overview: TWO EXCLUSIVE VILLAS NESTLED ON BRAČ ISLAND, CRAFTED FOR THOSE WHO SEEK PRIVACY, ELEGANCE, AND THE TIMELESS BEAUTY OF THE ADRIATIC SEA.
challenge: CRO Sea Villas had beautiful properties but no brand to stand behind them. In a crowded market of coastal rentals, guests decide in seconds whether a place feels trustworthy, and without a name, a visual identity or an online presence, the villas were easy to overlook. The challenge was to build a brand from the ground up that would feel genuinely premium without becoming flashy, and that could earn the trust of guests booking from far away before they had ever seen the place in person.
story: I started by getting to know the villas, the coastline and the kind of guest CRO Sea Villas wanted to attract. The exploration phase tested several directions before we settled on a logo that felt quiet, confident and unmistakably coastal. From there I expanded it into a full identity system, keeping it deliberately restrained so the places themselves could do the talking. The final step was carrying that system into marketing materials and preparing everything for print, so nothing got lost between screen and paper.
results: CRO Sea Villas started with beautiful properties and nothing around them: no brand, no visual language and no real online presence. Today they have a complete identity that guests can recognize and connect with before they ever arrive. It carries the same calm and quality as the villas themselves, so every touchpoint, online and in print, builds trust from the first glance. For a business that lives on first impressions, that difference is easy to see.

testimonial.quote: Dejan understood what we were about before he drew a single line. The exploration phase gave us directions we hadn’t considered, and the logo we chose felt right from the first time we saw it. He then built it into a full identity that’s calm and pared back, which suits a brand of luxury villas on the coast perfectly. When we extended the project to marketing materials and print, his knowledge of production really showed. Everything now feels like one brand, and we’d work with him again without hesitation.
testimonial.name: Ivan Leko

title: Falco Gin
overview: ART DIRECTED A PREMIUM PRINT BOOKLET BRIDGING FALCO GIN'S HERITAGE CRAFTSMANSHIP WITH A BOLD, CONTEMPORARY VISUAL IDENTITY.
challenge: Falco Gin had a logo and packaging, but nothing that held the brand together. There were no guidelines, no typographic system and no rules for colour, so every new piece had to be figured out from scratch. The project started with a simple request for a cocktail menu, but it quickly became clear that the brand needed a foundation before it could grow into print, retail and new markets with a consistent voice.
story: I began with the cocktail menu and used it to define what the brand had been missing. I set the typography and colour palette, adapted the existing logo so it worked across formats, and refined the packaging to sit within the same system. The layout language drew on the Swiss style: a strict grid, generous white space and an editorial feel. That system carried straight into the brochures and booklets that followed, so every printed piece felt like part of one brand.
results: What started as a single menu became a complete visual system that Falco Gin still builds on. The brand now speaks with one voice across packaging, print and online. Today Falco Gin is one of the better known gins in Switzerland and sells worldwide through its own online shop. A clear, recognisable identity has been part of that growth from the first bottle on the shelf to the last page of the booklet.

title: Adria Design Biennale
overview: ADRIA DESIGN BIENNALE 2026 IS A CONCEPTUAL IDENTITY SYSTEM CREATED FOR A MULTIDISCIPLINARY DESIGN FESTIVAL IN SPLIT, CROATIA, CONNECTING GRAPHIC DESIGN, MOTION, PRODUCT DESIGN, AND ARCHITECTURE THROUGH ONE UNIFIED VISUAL LANGUAGE.
challenge: A design festival has to speak to people who look at visual work for a living. It needs an identity bold enough to hold its own next to the work it presents, flexible enough to cover four disciplines at once, and rooted enough in its place that it could not belong to any other city. The brief I set myself was to build that system for a festival on the Adriatic coast, held among the stones of Diocletian's Palace.
story: The identity starts with the sea. Flowing, wave-like shapes run through every piece, set against a tight condensed wordmark and bold editorial typography that keeps the energy in check. A warm palette of coral red, deep teal and mustard gives each discipline its own voice while staying one family. I took the system across the full festival experience: speaker posters, tickets, a website, check-in walls and large banners hung between the columns of the palace, so the identity works from a phone screen to the scale of the city.

title: Pletho
overview: BRAND IDENTITY DESIGN FOR A HEALTH TECHNOLOGY STARTUP FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING ASSISTIVE PRODUCTS THAT IMPROVE EVERYDAY INDEPENDENCE FOR PEOPLE LIVING WITH MOTOR CONTROL CONDITIONS.
challenge: Pletho came to me as an idea and a brief, with nothing built yet. The founder was developing assistive products for people living with motor control conditions, a serious subject in a category where most brands look clinical and cold. The challenge was to create a complete brand from zero that would feel human, calm and trustworthy, without losing the credibility a health technology company needs in front of investors, partners and the people who would use the product.
story: Working from the founder's brief, I designed the logo and built the full identity system around it: typography, colour, brand guidelines and the rules that keep everything consistent. With the foundation in place, I carried the system into pitch decks for investor meetings, then into web design and the packaging for the product itself. Every decision was made to steer away from the look of a medical device and towards something warm, clear and easy to trust.
results: Pletho launched with a brand that does not look like a medical product. It feels warm and reassuring while the problem it solves is a serious one, and that balance is exactly what it needed. The identity, together with the pitch decks built on it, supported the startup through several important investment rounds. Years later those investments are still keeping the company going, and the brand still carries every part of it, from the first slide to the product box.

testimonial.quote: Dejan built Pletho's brand from nothing but an idea and a brief. He understood what we were trying to do faster than anyone we talked to, and turned something serious into a brand people actually trust. Investors noticed it, our users feel it, and years later we're still working together. I wouldn't trust anyone else with it.
testimonial.name: Thomas Wollenberger
